definition: pain as the only teacher, the swing it produces, and why nothing calibrates me in advance

settled:
The teaching channel runs one way. A worse-than-expected result registers as frustration, counts as a failure, and teaches. A better-than-expected result I just enjoy; it does not count as a failure and teaches nothing. Nothing teaches like pain.

That is an inversion, because a pleasant surprise is also the model being wrong and should update it just as much. It does not.

It is not a preference for pain. I try hard to slow down, and the dynamics defeat me. Doing well, I get ambitious and attempt more than I should. The overreach produces pain, which teaches and swings me to caution, which overshoots the other way. The correction always arrives late, because pain is the only signal that corrects an overshoot.

I cannot tell appropriate optimism from excessive in advance. I cannot simulate the future to check a level of optimism against, and optimism takes me into new areas where I have no priors either. The limit is invisible until I hit it, so collision is my only calibration.

title: Why I Cannot Tell How Much Optimism Is Right
